title: Repository & DbContext
blurb: The DbContext is a unit of work with a change tracker. Each entity moves through a little state machine — Added, Modified, Deleted, Unchanged, Detached — and a classic footgun (N+1) hides in innocent-looking loops.

docs.label: EF Core — Change tracking & entity states

levels.title: L1 · Entity state after a mutation
levels.prompt: An entity is loaded (tracked), then a property changes. Before SaveChanges, what's its EntityState?

blocks.label: Code

failStates.title: The tracker noticed
failStates.explain: Because the entity is tracked, mutating a property flips its state to Modified immediately — even before SaveChanges. SaveChanges is what writes it and resets it to Unchanged.

failStates.title: It already exists
failStates.explain: Added is for a brand-new entity passed to Add(). This one was loaded from the database, so editing it makes it Modified.

levels.title: L2 · AsNoTracking
levels.prompt: A no-tracking query, then a mutation, then SaveChanges. What persists?

blocks.label: Code

failStates.title: Nothing is tracking it
failStates.explain: AsNoTracking returns a Detached entity — the change tracker isn't watching it. SaveChanges has no recorded change for it, so the edit is silently lost.

failStates.title: No error — just a no-op
failStates.explain: SaveChanges doesn't throw; it simply has nothing to persist for a Detached entity. That silence is exactly why this bug is sneaky.

levels.title: L3 · The N+1 query
levels.prompt: This loop quietly fires a flood of SQL. Find the line that causes it and pick the fix.

payload.intro: One query loaded the orders. Then something inside the loop secretly runs another query per row.

fixes.label: Eager-load up front: ctx.Orders.Include(o => o.Customer).ThenInclude(c => c.Orders)
Call ToList() again inside the loop

failStates.title: The first query is fine
failStates.explain: Loading the orders is a single, healthy query. The N+1 happens where a navigation property (o.Customer...) is touched lazily inside the loop — one extra query per order.

failStates.title: The loop itself is innocent
failStates.explain: Iterating in memory costs nothing. It's the navigation-property access inside it that triggers a lazy query each pass.

failStates.title: AsNoTracking doesn't stop the N queries
failStates.explain: No-tracking helps memory and speed, but you still lazily load the Customer N times. You have to eager-load the navigation so it comes back in the first query.

failStates.title: That makes it worse
failStates.explain: Another ToList() inside the loop adds even more round-trips. The fix is to Include the navigation so EF fetches it once, up front.
